children: France’s current account deficit widened to a seasonally adjusted €4.7 billion in July 2026 from an upwardly revised €1.6 billion in the previous month.

It marked the largest shortfall since January 2023, driven by a wider goods deficit, which increased to €6.8 billion from €5.2 billion in June, and a narrower services surplus, which fell to €3.8 billion from €5.3 billion.
Moreover, the primary income surplus edged down to €3.3 billion from €3.4 billion.
Meanwhile, the secondary income deficit remained unchanged at €5.0 billion.
For the first seven months of the year, France recorded a cumulative current account deficit of €12.0 billion, compared with €18.2 billion in the corresponding period of the previous year.

title: France Current Account Deficit Largest Since 2023
